hypothesis: A cheap reference-free runtime proxy (per-head live preceding-context K-variance) predicts per-head splice drift, enabling an online micro-gate.
findings: The reference-free proxy does not predict drift: mean Spearman rho = 0.193 (< 0.40 target).
Mean per-head drift is nearly constant (91-105) across all depths and both on-/off-topic contexts, so there is no per-request variance for a scalar-threshold gate to discriminate.
Phase 1's depth-adaptive recompute already repairs this drift (capstone: top-1 held, KL to 0 at all depths).
decision: Ship only the cache-line alignment hardening (Component A); do not ship the online micro-gate. Keep the deterministic depth-adaptive recompute curve as the Path-A<->B repair mechanism.
